principles.text: Copywriting is sales on paper: it scales your one-to-one selling to an unlimited audience.
Go where your target readers already are, make content that wins there, and siphon them to your list.
Get a sale within days, by cold email, phone and a payment link, before a website, LLC or product.
Charge more than you think: a higher price funds a good service and pays to acquire customers.
Working on one good business for 10 years will likely beat 10 decent things for a year each.

sampleQA.question: How do I grow a newsletter from zero without an ad budget?

answer.text: Start with distribution: before you have an article idea, decide who you want to reach and where they already are.
Write posts built to rank in specific communities like subreddits and Hacker News, then convert that traffic with a strong pop-up.
Make the forgotten text good too, like thank-you pages and welcome emails, and spend real time on headlines, since they can move click-through from 1% to 10%.
Hold off on paid marketing until you have about 20,000 to 40,000 people. Then work out what a subscriber is worth and buy ads up to your payback window.

sampleQA.question: How do I test an idea before building it?

answer.text: Use back-of-the-envelope math and check that a big player exists, which shows the market is large enough. Detailed spreadsheets this early are procrastination driven by fear.
Research by cold-calling bankers, founders and ex-employees, and by reading reviews.
Launch with a Google Doc and a Typeform, or post a public offer and count replies, then call every lead personally and take payment through a simple link.
Make at least $100 in sales before you buy a domain name.

sampleQA.question: Should I bootstrap or raise venture capital?

answer.text: If your main goal is freedom and making money for yourself, bootstrap. VC fits founders who want to go huge, so pick deliberately.
Your cap table is one of the few business mistakes you can't undo, and raising commits you to optimizing for investor returns.
Choose a model that doesn't need outside money. Hampton charges up front and reached millions in run rate before it had a website.
